issues.label: 1c
issues.detail: Model answer claims loudness increases 'by the same factor' (4×) when amplitude increases 4×. Physically, loudness (perceived intensity) is logarithmic; intensity is proportional to amplitude squared. Amplitude 4× → intensity 16×, not 4×.
issues.correction: Model answer should state: 'Loudness will increase significantly. Loudness is related to the intensity of the sound wave, which depends on amplitude squared. Increasing amplitude by a factor of 4 increases intensity by a factor of 16, making the sound much louder.'

issues.label: 2c
issues.detail: Model answer incorrectly states loudness increases 'by a factor of 4' when amplitude increases 4×. Same error as 1c: intensity ∝ amplitude², so 4× amplitude → 16× intensity.
issues.correction: Model answer should state: 'Loudness will increase significantly because intensity is proportional to amplitude squared. Increasing amplitude by a factor of 4 increases intensity by a factor of 16.'

issues.label: 3a
issues.detail: Model answer gives 70.7 cm³ but calculation shown is π(1.5)²(10) = π(2.25)(10) = 70.685... ≈ 70.7 cm³. Rounding is acceptable but inconsistent with later parts using 70.65 cm³.
issues.correction: Use consistent rounding: either 70.7 cm³ or 70.65 cm³ throughout all related questions. Recommend 70.7 cm³ (2 s.f. appropriate for given data).

issues.label: 4c
issues.detail: Model answer states loudness 'would also increase' without quantifying. Same amplitude-loudness error: intensity ∝ amplitude², not linearly.
issues.correction: Model answer should clarify: 'Loudness will increase significantly. Since intensity is proportional to amplitude squared, increasing amplitude by a factor of 4 increases intensity by a factor of 16, making the sound much louder.'

issues.label: 5a
issues.detail: Model answer gives 70.65 cm³ but uses π without specifying value. Calculation: π(1.5)²(10) = 70.685... Rounding differs from question 3a (70.7 cm³).
issues.correction: Standardize: state 'V = π(1.5)²(10) ≈ 70.7 cm³' or consistently use 70.65 cm³ across all cylinder questions.

issues.label: 6a
issues.detail: Model answer uses π = 3.14 explicitly, giving 70.65 cm³. This differs from questions 3a/5a which use π ≈ 3.14159, yielding 70.7 cm³. Inconsistent precision across identical scenarios.
issues.correction: Standardize all cylinder volume calculations to use same π value and rounding convention across questions 3a, 5a, 6a, 10a, 15a, 18a.

issues.label: 8c
issues.detail: Model answer: 'Loudness would increase significantly...increasing amplitude by a factor of 4 would make the sound much louder.' Lacks quantitative relationship; intensity ∝ amplitude², so 4× amplitude → 16× intensity.
issues.correction: Add: 'Since intensity is proportional to amplitude squared, a 4× increase in amplitude results in a 16× increase in intensity.'

issues.label: 11c
issues.detail: Model answer: 'Increasing amplitude by a factor of 4 will increase loudness.' Vague; does not explain intensity ∝ amplitude² relationship.
issues.correction: Clarify: 'Loudness increases significantly because intensity is proportional to amplitude squared. A 4× amplitude increase produces a 16× intensity increase.'

issues.label: 12c

issues.correction: Add: 'Since intensity is proportional to amplitude squared, increasing amplitude by a factor of 4 increases intensity by a factor of 16.'

review.summary: Assessment contains 51 questions across density/floating and sound properties. Main issues: systematic errors in amplitude-loudness relationship (10 questions incorrectly state linear proportionality instead of intensity ∝ amplitude²); inconsistent π rounding in cylinder volumes; unit conversion error in 20a (off by factor 100); incomplete question 14. No missing data or repeated identical questions detected.
